text.content:
Create an enemy from the Actors sidebar's Create Actor button with Type set to NPC / Adversary (or Monster, which adds the Monster Creator). Every enemy has a Grade — Mook, Normal or Elite — and a battlefield Role (Defender, Striker, Controller, Blaster, Support, Skirmisher). Grade decides how the enemy is run:

  • Mooks and Normals use the reduced engine: no dice Pools and no Resources. Their sheet is a compact record — Grade, Role, Wounds, printed Defenses, Resilience, Movement, Senses and Abilities — plus their printed allowances: Initiative dice (2d10), Actions per Turn (Mook 1, Normal 2), Reactions per Round and Task Dice (4 or 5). Leave an allowance blank to use the Grade default. A GM toggle reveals Attributes, Styles and cards for hand-building.
  • Elites use the full engine like a character: Pools of 6, printed card costs, and an optional printed Roll Limit.

Abilities are the enemy's printed moves. Each has a kind (Action, Reaction, Triggered or Passive), its printed dice, the Defense it rolls against or an unopposed flag, and a frequency: At Will, once per Round, or a number of uses between Recoveries. The Recovery button refreshes limited uses; nothing else does, not even a new Combat.

The Starting Enemy Examples compendium holds the ten playtest profiles from the rulebook (three Mooks, four Normals, three Elites). Import one and change its fiction freely.

Leave enemy tokens unlinked (Foundry's default) so several copies track their own Wounds. Character tokens are force-linked instead.

Portrait Art vs. Token Art

Every Actor has two images: the sheet Portrait (click the header art) and the canvas Token Image (the pawn icon on the Portrait's corner). Foundry copies the Portrait into the Token Image the first time you set one; after that they are independent. Since enemy tokens are unlinked, a new Token Image only affects tokens placed afterwards.

Enemies are compact profiles, not characters. Wound capacity by Grade: Mook 2, Normal 4, Elite 5. All three are Defeated when their capacity fills; they use no severity spaces, Wound Cards or Death Track. A Defeated enemy is unconscious and dying unless Stabilize or a nonlethal hit made it stable (the header reads "Defeated (stable)").

Reduced engine (Mooks and Normals)

Initiative is a plain 2d10 roll, made automatically when you roll from the tracker. Each Turn grants the printed Actions; each Round the printed Reactions, refreshed at the start of every Round. Abilities roll their printed dice against the named Defense with the normal Success Die and Surges. There are no Pools, so Dazed's burn and the unaware surcharge are waived. One utility Basic Action per Turn (Dash, Reconfigure, Stabilize or Perform Task, including Help) spends an Action and costs no dice. Basic Melee Attack, Basic Ranged Attack, Defend and Prepare Action need explicit permission, so the sheet refuses them and the Monster Creator never picks them. For an uncertain task, Roll Task Dice against a Difficulty. The sheet warns when an allowance is exceeded rather than blocking, since profiles control exceptions.

Elites

Elites pay card costs from Pools. An ability's printed dice are its minimum commitment, paid through the usual prompt with the profile's Roll Limit shown as advice. Task Dice fall back to the Roll Limit.

Planning

Encounter categories by target length: Minor 1–2 Rounds, Severe 2–3, Critical 3–5, Boss usually 3–5 with a Leader or Solo structure. A short Adventure has about 1–2 meaningful combats, a medium one 2–4, a long one 4–6 or more separated by Recovery opportunities. Team Tier is not an enemy rating; pick opposition for the story.

Combat runs entirely through Foundry's own Combat Tracker — add combatants, click Begin Combat, and advance rounds and turns from there. Every way of rolling Initiative opens the same commit prompt for characters and Elites (1 die up to the base pool); Mooks and Normals roll 2d10 with no prompt. Combatants sort by total, then Success Die, then Grace.

The tracker runs each Turn's bookkeeping: Pools form and clear, prepared Actions expire, accumulated Damage resets, Dazed burns, reduced-engine allowances refresh, and the Death Track advances for a Dying character. End of Turn settles Gestalt upkeep and Combo, then forms the Reaction Pool.

Deleting the Combat does not end the fictional Encounter: anything scoped to the Encounter — Threads, Authority, Locks, Combo, Contingencies, Stance and Unstable, per-Encounter Card cooldowns, an active Full Manifestation — stays until a sheet's own New Encounter button is clicked. Use it once the table agrees the Encounter, not just one bout of Combat, is over.

Conditions live in the Conditions compendium and double as Token HUD status icons — right-click a token, open its status-effects palette, and toggle a Condition directly. This adds or removes a real owned Condition item on the Actor with its mechanical effect (Exposed's −1 to all Defenses, for instance), exactly the same as dragging the Condition onto the sheet. The sheet's + Add button on the Conditions row does the same from a picker. Each Condition Item carries a Classification (Ordinary/Specialty/Wound/Influence Consequence/Cover/Other) purely as a label.

Stacking, Reapplication, and Participation

Differently named Conditions stack. The same named ordinary Condition does not stack with itself — reapplying it refreshes or extends its duration without shortening what remains. Ordinary Condition removal never removes a Wound Card, a Specialty Condition, Strain or Manifestation Wounds unless it explicitly says it can. A Condition restricts only what its own entry names; the character keeps their remaining Actions, Reactions and Movement.

Authoring New Content

If you have Foundry's "Create Items" permission, a wand-icon scene-control button opens the Create Content wizard for building new Action/Reaction Cards, Equipment, and Conditions straight into the compendium. For adding many at once, use its Bulk Import option: download a CSV template, fill it out, and upload it.

Compendiums

Species, Heritages, Distinctions, the Starting Enemy Examples and the Full Manifestation profiles are hand-authored from the v0.6 rulebook. The Combat Styles Reference and Full Manifestation Guide journals document their mechanics in full.

The Monster Creator's Auto-Generate Stat Block button fills a hand-built Elite (or a full-stats Mook or Normal) from a tunable budget table, then hands every result back for you to edit. Defaults match the rulebook's Starting Enemy Examples:

GradeAttributesStylesResilienceTemp WoundsCards (A/R)EquipmentWounds
Mook2 pts, max 22 pts, max 2001 / 012
Normal7 pts, max 35 pts, max 3102 / 124
Elite13 pts, max 512 pts, max 5204 / 345

Auto-Generate rolls, in order: a weighted Attribute/Style point-buy (leaning toward the domain you pick as Emphasis and respecting the five Distinction gates), Resilience and Temporary Wounds from the table, qualifying Combat Cards weighted toward the highest Styles (never Basic Melee Attack, Basic Ranged Attack, Defend or Prepare Action, which enemies need permission for), and a random Equipment draw. Each step has its own Reroll button.

Treat the table as a starting point — the examples run Resilience 0 for Mooks, 1–2 for Normals and 2–3 for Elites. Every number is in the Grade Budgets system setting and takes effect immediately.

Create one Team actor per party and link each character to it. The Team sheet holds Team Tier (1 to 5) and the Team record: identity, Major Goal, methods and principles; Things and Commitments tagged Asset, Obligation, Borrowed or Pledged; and Organizations as Friendly, Neutral or Hostile. Track what matters at the current scale, not every possession.

Team Tier is lasting Campaign progression and only increases, when you judge the Campaign ready for a broader scope. There is no point threshold. Raising it on the Team sheet clears every member's remaining Temporary Influence; it refunds no spent Influence, clears no Core consequences, and grants no personal dice, cards or capacity. Tier never rates a character's competence or an enemy's strength.

Acquisition

Through routine channels a character can obtain a Chassis or Fitting whose Component Tier is no higher than Team Tier (each Component checked separately, up to Tier 5) when a supplier exists. The Equipment tab flags Components above the Team's Tier as exceptional; obtained gear is always usable and keeps no rent. Personal Reach absorbs the Influence pressure of a significant acquisition; it does not by itself open higher-Tier suppliers. Quartermaster's Due grants one Chassis and one Fitting up to 1 Tier above Team Tier at creation.

Judging scale

Use these reference anchors for a noticeable expense: Tier 1 about $100, Tier 2 $1,000, Tier 3 $10,000, Tier 4 $100,000, Tier 5 $1,000,000. Routine expenses below the scale create no pressure; a meaningful one near the anchor is 1 ordinary pressure; a heavier commitment can be several. Printed Influence costs keep their stated amounts at every Tier.
